growth and profitability are positively correlated, that this relationship is stronger during economic crisis, that export intensity moderates the growth-profitability relationship and that innovation does not play an important role.

the growth-profitability relationship in the economic crisis context is asymmetric, with the impact of profits on growth being stronger than the effect of growth on profit, and that the role of export intensity as moderator of this relationship is more relevant than that of innovation efforts.
growth and profitability are positively inter-related, but the effect of growth on profitability is stronger than the effect of profitability on growth.

the relationship between growth and profitability, a relationship that has been studied by several authors, but it is the first time it is analyzed in a dynamic framework and in an economic crisis period, taking into account the endogeneity of the relationship.
the dynamics between growth rates and profit margins in a context of economic crisis.
the dynamics between growth-profitability, the role of innovation in this relationship, and the moderating effect of export intensity in a context of economic crisis.

the growth of firms in the economic crisis has been mainly achieved through exports.

firms that have managed to maintain their growth in the crisis have been those with higher export intensity.
the growth-profit relationship is not a unidirectional relationship.
